name: Yaps
summary: Voice tools that run on your own device: dictation into any app, transcription of audio and video files with SRT captions, read-aloud voices and voice notes. Free on Android, iPhone and iPad; the desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux need Yaps Pro.
best_for: writers, students and professionals who dictate or transcribe every day and want the speech processing on their own computer, across Windows, macOS and Linux
skip_if: you want a one-time purchase rather than a subscription, or you need a finished Windows version today
honest_knock: The desktop trial converts to a paid plan automatically, and the terms exclude refunds solely because you forgot to cancel; uninstalling the app does not cancel the subscription either. Windows is still labelled beta. 'On-device' has limits: signing in, billing, sync and model downloads use the internet, and on iPhone and iPad the system speech service can fall back to Apple's remote recognition.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Yaps Pro · per year, annual billing, shown as $12 a month, for the desktop apps
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-26 on yaps.ai/pricing with annual billing selected; the monthly price was read on 2026-10-16; dollar amounts, the page does not name the currency) Yaps is free on Android, iPhone and iPad: voice typing in other apps, voice notes with local search and read-aloud with 4 voices, without an account or card. Yaps Pro covers the desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux and costs $144 a year (shown as $12 a month) or $15 billed month to month. Pro adds unlimited dictation and read-aloud, unlimited transcription of audio and video files, SRT captions, speaker identification on Windows and macOS, chat with your notes, 18 voices, the Studio editor and vault sync. Desktop starts with a 7-day free trial that converts to the paid plan unless you cancel. Enterprise is priced on request. Students with a verified .edu address get 50% off the first year of annual Pro ($72), then the full price.

claims.claim: Free audio to text, without the upload.
claims.observed: The tool transcribed the file in the page after downloading a model to the browser; no sign-in was asked. The network traffic was not inspected, so it is not proven that the audio was never uploaded.
claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The headline of the tool page against what the page showed; no network log was read.
claims.buying_consequence: You can transcribe a short file for free without an account; that the audio stays on your machine is the claim of the site and was not checked by us.

claims.claim: The model download is about 80MB. Your browser may cache it for later visits.
claims.observed: With the Balanced model (80MB, the default) the file field was usable about 16 seconds after the start (13:18:07 to about 13:18:23, judged from two looks). A second visit with a cached model was not tried.
claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The warning on the page against one load on one connection; the Fast model of 44MB was not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: The first run waits for a download of about 80MB, which took about 16 seconds here.

claims.observed: The file of 10 seconds was loaded at 13:18:31 and the transcript was on screen within 10 seconds, with the counter 23 WORDS 9S. It took 3 steps: leave the model, choose the file, read the result.
claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The counter on the result against our own clock for one 10 second clip; longer files were not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: A short clip is turned into text in seconds once the model is loaded.

claims.claim: This is the short test recording for a transcription tool, where order 12 blue snowboards on Monday, and the invoice number is 4472.
claims.observed: Against the spoken text there were 2 word errors (a became the, We became where) and a full stop became a comma. The numbers were written as digits and were right: twelve became 12 and four four seven two became 4472.
claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: Our own spoken text against the transcript of one synthetic clip; the site states no accuracy figure to compare with.
claims.buying_consequence: On a clear voice the numbers came out right, but a whole word changed meaning (We became where), so read the transcript before you use it.

claims.observed: The buttons Copy, Download .txt, Download timestamped and Download .srt are on the result page, and the timestamped view showed segments at [00:00] and [00:06]. Nothing was downloaded, so the SRT file was not seen.
claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The export buttons against files that were not downloaded; no SRT file was opened.
claims.buying_consequence: The browser tool offers subtitle export, but whether the SRT file is correct is not confirmed.

claims.claim: It can't tell you who was speaking.
claims.observed: The browser tool gives an unlabelled transcript and says that speaker labels are part of the Yaps desktop transcription. The test clip had one voice, so this limit did not change the result.
claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The text under the result against a transcript without speaker labels; the desktop app was not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: For meetings or interviews the free browser tool will not label speakers; that needs the paid desktop app.

claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The Pro feature list against a desktop app that was out of scope.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether the desktop app tells speakers apart well is not confirmed by this test.

claims.plan: No plan or trial was started; the pricing page was read on Annual and Monthly without clicking
claims.comparability: The Free plan lines against a test of the browser tool; the mobile apps were out of scope.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session tested only the free browser tool Audio to text of Yaps, without an account and not the desktop app. After a model download of about 80MB that took about 16 seconds, a 10 second synthetic clip was transcribed in the browser within 10 seconds. The text had 2 word errors (a became the, We became where) and the numbers were right (12 and 4472). The tool has a timestamped view and buttons for TXT and SRT, which were not used, and it says it cannot tell who was speaking: speaker labels are only in the paid desktop app. Nothing was bought. Scope: this test covers ONLY the free browser tool Audio to text on yaps.ai. The Yaps desktop app (dictation, file transcription, speaker labels) and the mobile apps were not downloaded, installed or tried. Account and start: NO account was made and none was used; the browser tool runs without signing in. Our AI assistant ran the test in our own tab of our browser, starting at 13:18:07, on yaps.ai/tools/audio-to-text. Nothing was installed and no e-mail address, phone number, password or card was typed in. The cookie banner was set to Decline. The dossier name is Yaps and the review is on AIBM (yaps-review). Core action: the page says Free audio to text, without the upload, and shows that it runs on your machine with no upload and no signup. The model choice is Fast, English only, 44MB or Balanced, multilingual, 80MB (Balanced was the default) and the language was English. The page warns that the model download is about 80MB, that the browser may cache it, and that startup still takes time. Loading the model took about 16 seconds (13:18:07 to about 13:18:23, judged from two looks, not a stopwatch); it is a download by the web page, not an install. The file test-spraak.m4a (41 KB, 10 seconds of a synthetic macOS voice reading a made up text with no personal data) was loaded at 13:18:31, and within 10 seconds the text was on screen. The counter said 23 WORDS 9S. It took 3 steps: leave the model as it is, choose the file, read the result. Result: This is the short test recording for a transcription tool, where order 12 blue snowboards on Monday, and the invoice number is 4472. The spoken text was: This is a short test recording for a transcription tool. We order twelve blue snowboards on Monday, and the invoice number is four four seven two. So there were 2 word errors (a became the, We became where) and the full stop after tool became a comma; the numbers were turned into digits and were right (12 and 4472). The view With timestamps showed two segments, at [00:00] and [00:06]. The buttons Copy, Download .txt, Download timestamped and Download .srt are there, but nothing was downloaded, so the content of the SRT file was not checked. Under the result the page says It can't tell you who was speaking: speaker labels are only in the desktop app. An e-mail field for product updates was not used. Plans: The pricing page yaps.ai/pricing was read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 and read again just before this delivery the same day, with the same prices: Free $0 /forever (mobile only: voice typing in apps on Android, iPhone and iPad, voice notes with local search, read aloud with 4 mobile voices, runs on-device, no account needed); Yaps Pro $12 /month billed annually ($144/year) or $15 /month billed monthly, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a 7-day free trial that then renews until cancelled (unlimited dictation, transcription of audio and video files, video captions exported as SRT, speaker identification on Windows and macOS, 18 voices); Enterprise Custom. The amounts match the dossier ($144 a year, $15 a month, 7-day trial). No payment screen was opened and the desktop app was not downloaded. Cancelling: there is no account and no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel. Not tested: the desktop app (dictation, files, speaker labels), the mobile apps, the SRT file itself, the multilingual mode and the Fast model (44MB), the payment screen and the conversion of the trial. Clean up: there is no account and no test data was left behind; our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The browser tool first downloads a model of about 80MB, so the first run takes some seconds before you can pick a file. On a clear synthetic voice it still made 2 word errors in one sentence (We became where), so you should read a transcript before you use it. It cannot tell speakers apart; that is part of the desktop app, which is a subscription with a trial that renews until cancelled, not a one-time purchase.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session tested only the free browser tool Audio to text of Yaps, without an account and not the desktop app. After a model download of about 80MB that took about 16 seconds, a 10 second synthetic clip was transcribed in the browser within 10 seconds. The text had 2 word errors (a became the, We became where) and the numbers were right (12 and 4472). The tool has a timestamped view and buttons for TXT and SRT, which were not used, and it says it cannot tell who was speaking: speaker labels are only in the paid desktop app. Nothing was bought. Scope: this test covers ONLY the free browser tool Audio to text on yaps.ai. The Yaps desktop app (dictation, file transcription, speaker labels) and the mobile apps were not downloaded, installed or tried. Account and start: NO account was made and none was used; the browser tool runs without signing in. Our AI assistant ran the test in our own tab of our browser, starting at 13:18:07, on yaps.ai/tools/audio-to-text. Nothing was installed and no e-mail address, phone number, password or card was typed in. The cookie banner was set to Decline. The dossier name is Yaps and the review is on AIBM (yaps-review). Core action: the page says Free audio to text, without the upload, and shows that it runs on your machine with no upload and no signup. The model choice is Fast, English only, 44MB or Balanced, multilingual, 80MB (Balanced was the default) and the language was English. The page warns that the model download is about 80MB, that the browser may cache it, and that startup still takes time. Loading the model took about 16 seconds (13:18:07 to about 13:18:23, judged from two looks, not a stopwatch); it is a download by the web page, not an install. The file test-spraak.m4a (41 KB, 10 seconds of a synthetic macOS voice reading a made up text with no personal data) was loaded at 13:18:31, and within 10 seconds the text was on screen. The counter said 23 WORDS 9S. It took 3 steps: leave the model as it is, choose the file, read the result. Result: This is the short test recording for a transcription tool, where order 12 blue snowboards on Monday, and the invoice number is 4472. The spoken text was: This is a short test recording for a transcription tool. We order twelve blue snowboards on Monday, and the invoice number is four four seven two. So there were 2 word errors (a became the, We became where) and the full stop after tool became a comma; the numbers were turned into digits and were right (12 and 4472). The view With timestamps showed two segments, at [00:00] and [00:06]. The buttons Copy, Download .txt, Download timestamped and Download .srt are there, but nothing was downloaded, so the content of the SRT file was not checked. Under the result the page says It can't tell you who was speaking: speaker labels are only in the desktop app. An e-mail field for product updates was not used. Plans: The pricing page yaps.ai/pricing was read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 and read again just before this delivery the same day, with the same prices: Free $0 /forever (mobile only: voice typing in apps on Android, iPhone and iPad, voice notes with local search, read aloud with 4 mobile voices, runs on-device, no account needed); Yaps Pro $12 /month billed annually ($144/year) or $15 /month billed monthly, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a 7-day free trial that then renews until cancelled (unlimited dictation, transcription of audio and video files, video captions exported as SRT, speaker identification on Windows and macOS, 18 voices); Enterprise Custom. The amounts match the dossier ($144 a year, $15 a month, 7-day trial). No payment screen was opened and the desktop app was not downloaded. Cancelling: there is no account and no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel. Not tested: the desktop app (dictation, files, speaker labels), the mobile apps, the SRT file itself, the multilingual mode and the Fast model (44MB), the payment screen and the conversion of the trial. Clean up: there is no account and no test data was left behind; our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The browser tool first downloads a model of about 80MB, so the first run takes some seconds before you can pick a file. On a clear synthetic voice it still made 2 word errors in one sentence (We became where), so you should read a transcript before you use it. It cannot tell speakers apart; that is part of the desktop app, which is a subscription with a trial that renews until cancelled, not a one-time purchase.
